title: Arithmetic and Geometric Series
seo_title: Arithmetic and Geometric Series Worksheet: Sigma Notation, Infinite Series (Algebra 2) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems. For example, calculate mortgage payments.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 2 worksheet on series: sigma notation, arithmetic series, finite and infinite geometric series and word problems like salaries and bouncing balls. 100 questions.
key_big: Arithmetic: S = n(a₁ + aₙ)/2. Geometric: S = a₁(1 − rⁿ)/(1 − r).
key_sub: An infinite geometric series has a sum a₁/(1 − r) only when |r| < 1.
body_html:
How it works

A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence. Summation (sigma) notation lists the terms to add: write each term for k = the start value up to the end value.

  • Arithmetic series: Sn = n(a1 + an)/2, where an = a1 + (n − 1)d.
  • Geometric series: Sn = a1(1 − rn)/(1 − r).
  • Infinite geometric series: if |r| < 1, the sum is a1/(1 − r). If |r| ≥ 1, there is no sum.
Example

Find 3 + 7 + 11 + … for 20 terms.

a20 = 3 + 19(4) = 79

S = 20(3 + 79)/2

Answer: 820

Example

Find 12 + 6 + 3 + …

r = 1/2

12 ÷ (1 − 1/2)

Answer: 24

Common mistakes

  • Counting terms wrong: k = 3 to 8 has 6 terms, not 5.
  • Using the last term instead of the number of terms for n.
  • Giving the nth term when the question asks for the sum.
  • Finding an infinite sum when |r| ≥ 1. It does not exist.

faq.q: What is the formula for an arithmetic series?
faq.a: S_n = n(a_1 + a_n)/2. Average the first and last terms and multiply by the number of terms.

faq.q: What is the formula for a finite geometric series?
faq.a: S_n = a_1(1 − r^n)/(1 − r), where r is the common ratio and n is the number of terms.

faq.q: When does an infinite geometric series have a sum?
faq.a: Only when |r| < 1. Then the sum is a_1/(1 − r).
Σ means add. The numbers below and above the sigma give the first and last values of the index k.
